fields.verbatim_quote: Under the current rules and geopolitical landscape, we are unable to create and deliver a competitive product for China's data center market that receives approval from both the USG and the Chinese government. As of the end of fiscal year 2026, we were effectively foreclosed from competing in China's data center computing/compute market, and our effective foreclosure from the China market helped our competitors build larger developer and customer ecosystems to challenge us worldwide.

numeric_signal.note: H20 inventory charge in Q1 FY2026 due to export control restrictions

fields.verbatim_quote: In April 2025, the USG informed us that it requires a license for export to China (including Hong Kong and Macau) and D:5 countries, or to companies headquartered or with an ultimate parent therein, of our H20 integrated circuits and any other circuits achieving the H20's memory bandwidth, interconnect bandwidth, or combination thereof. As a result of these requirements, we incurred a $4.5 billion charge in the first quarter of fiscal year 2026 associated with H20 for excess inventory and purchase obligations, as the demand for H20 products diminished.

We utilize foundries, such as Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited, or TSMC, and Samsung Electronics Co., Ltd., or Samsung, to produce our semiconductor wafers. We purchase memory from SK Hynix Inc., Micron Technology, Inc., and Samsung. We utilize CoWoS technology for semiconductor packaging. We engage with independent subcontractors and contract manufacturers such as Hon Hai Precision Industry Co., Ltd., Wistron Corporation, and Fabrinet to perform assembly, testing and packaging of our final products.

In February 2026, the USG granted a license that would allow us to ship small amounts of H200 products to specific China-based customers. To date, we have not generated any revenue under the H200 licensing program, and do not yet know whether any imports will be allowed into China. The license requires that the H200s go through an inspection process in the United States prior to any shipment to the customer. As a result, any H200 shipped under the new licensing program will be subject to a 25% tariff upon importation into the United States.

fields.category: Market Competition & Loss of Market Share
fields.verbatim_quote: Our competitive position has been harmed by export controls, and our competitive position and future results will be further harmed, over the long term, if the restrictions remain in place or are expanded in geographic, customer, or product scope, if customers purchase product from competitors, if customers develop their own internal solution, if we are unable to provide contractual warranty or other extended service obligations, if the USG does not grant licenses in a timely manner or denies licenses to significant customers or if we incur significant transition costs.

The Chinese government has encouraged customers to purchase from our China-based competitors and discouraged customers from purchasing, importing, or using our data center products, including any China-specific product designed to comply with U.S. export controls.

In January 2025, the USG published the AI Diffusion IFR in the Federal Register. The IFR would have imposed a worldwide licensing requirement on our data center products, such as our H200, GB200 and GB300. The AI Diffusion IFR would have divided the world into three tiers, relegating most countries to "Tier 2" status, and would have created a complex and burdensome scheme for licensing approvals. In May 2025, the USG announced that it would rescind the AI Diffusion IFR and implement a replacement rule. The scope, timing, and requirements of the forthcoming rule remain uncertain.

financial_statements_and_notes.notes:
[chunk 1/2] KEY FINDINGS FROM NVIDIA FY2026 10-K FINANCIAL STATEMENTS & NOTES:

1. GROQ $13B INVESTMENT (CRITICAL): Cash flow statement explicitly line-items "Groq, Inc. $(13,000)" under investing activities, representing a $13B single investment in FY2026. Total non-marketable equity securities surged from $3.387B to $22.251B (+$18.864B YoY), with $17.502B in total non-marketable equity purchases in FY2026.

2. SUPPLY OBLIGATION OVERHANG ($95.2B): Outstanding inventory purchase and long-term supply/capacity obligations reached $95.2B against $21.4B in current inventory. PwC flagged this as a Critical Audit Matter due to significant management judgment in demand forecasting and export restriction impacts.

3. CIRCULAR INVESTOR-CUSTOMER DYNAMIC: NVIDIA is simultaneously (a) the dominant GPU/compute supplier to AI companies, (b) a major equity investor in those same AI companies (e.g., Groq), and (c) recognizing $8.918B in investment gains from those positions. This creates a structural circularity where revenue growth inflates investee valuations which flow back as NVIDIA income.

4. GOODWILL JUMP ($5.2B → $20.8B): Goodwill nearly quadrupled in FY2026, suggesting significant unannounced or undisclosed acquisitions beyond the $1.535B "acquisitions net of cash" in the cash flow statement. This section does not yet contain Note details explaining the delta — flags COST_OPACITY risk pending further note disclosure.

5. OPERATING LEASE EXPOSURE: $2.867B in operating lease assets and $2.572B in long-term operating lease liabilities represent off-balance-sheet-style obligations not classified as debt. Terms and any residual value guarantees not disclosed in this section.

6. NOTE: The filing section provided covers only the primary financial statements and Note 1 (accounting policies). Notes 7-12 (non-marketable equity securities detail, commitments, related parties) were not included. The $22.251B non-marketable equity portfolio likely contains additional named investees (CoreWeave, Lambda, xAI, Mistral, etc.) that would be extractable from Note 8. Only Groq is explicitly named in the cash flow statement in this section.
